_comment: Copy to params.prod.json (or params.staging.json) and fill in. Keys match the
Parameters block in template.yaml; anything omitted keeps the template default.
NO SECRETS BELONG HERE. The Google service-account key and the Transport Pro
password live in Secrets Manager — the stack creates both as empty placeholders
and deploy.ps1 prints the put-secret-value commands to fill them.
Keys beginning with an underscore are ignored by the deploy scripts.
_GmailUser: A real user, not the group. Google Groups cannot be impersonated, so read a member's mailbox and let GmailQuery narrow it to group mail.
_FetchLimit: 5, not the local 10. The turn budget scales with load count, so ten multi-load emails can exceed Lambda's 15-minute cap. Raise only after measuring.
_BedrockModelId: Verified present and ACTIVE on 2026-08-13. Confirm against your own account — the version suffix is not universal (sonnet-5 has none, sonnet-4-5 is ...-20250929-v1:0), and a wrong id deploys cleanly then fails at the first model call. Model access must be enabled by hand first — README.md step 1.
_RosterBucket: Where factoring_domains.json and carrier_contacts.json live. Blank disables BOTH fetches and the inline PAYBOT_FACTORING_DOMAINS / PAYBOT_CARRIER_CONTACTS entries stand alone.
_CarrierContactsKey: Exact addresses authorised for one carrier's loads, on top of the back office record. Hand-maintained — there is no generator, because the point of an entry is that the record does NOT hold the address. Upload it alongside the roster; blank disables the fetch.
_CargoTelReferralContacts: JSON list of "Name <address>" entries. Non-empty: every 6-digit-only email gets a deterministic hand-off reply naming these people, Cc'ing them — no scrape, no cross-checks, no model call. Wins over CargoTelReplies for 6-digit-only mail; mixed emails keep existing behaviour. Empty = today's behaviour (and the rollback).
_CargoTelCookieBucket: The login bot's bucket, not ours. The stack grants read on this one key only. If it is in another AWS account, that account must also allow this role — see README.md.
_AutoAddFactoringDomains: Auto-roster an unknown factoring sender and answer, instead of escalating. Left OFF here deliberately: it is the switch that turns the roster from 'domains somebody verified' into 'domains that wrote in and named a factor already on the load'. Read payment_bot.roster_candidate before enabling. An auto-added entry is marked AUTO-ADDED in factoring_domains_manual.json and logged as auto_roster_entry_added, so audit those and revoke what does not belong. IMPORTANT: this also means the roster bucket object drifts from what the generator produces — re-upload after a regeneration or auto-added entries are lost.
_LlmIdFilter: off | shadow | enforce. The model may only REMOVE load-id candidates the regex produced, never add one, and any failure leaves them unchanged. Left at shadow here so a new stack measures before it acts — read the id_filter_shadow log lines, then flip to enforce. Reading PDF attachments made the regex's precision problem materially worse (an invoice packet contributes its own invoice, rate-con, PRO and reference numbers), which is what enforce absorbs.
_NoaAttachmentReplies: Draft past an ATTACHED NOA, as opposed to the NOA WORDING SensitiveNoaReplies covers. Factors attach their NOA to routine rate verifications as standard, so 'false' escalates every one of them unanswered. The NOA still needs a human to file; the reply is forbidden from claiming it was filed.
_FactoringPrenoaReplies: Authorise a roster-verified factor on a load showing NO factor on file — the pre-funding flow. 'false' DENIES those senders outright, which is a large share of inbound factoring mail. Both of these were missing from the template until 2026-08-15, so a deployed stack ran with them off while .env had them on.
_ReplyCc: JSON list, never a bare address — reply_cc is a tuple setting, and a non-JSON value kills the worker at startup with SettingsError.
_ApprovalMode: drafts | chat (docs/CHAT_APPROVAL_PLAN.md). Keep at drafts until cutover step 4: with a ChatSpace set this is shadow mode — cards for visibility, Gmail Drafts unchanged. Flipping back to drafts is the whole rollback.
_Reviewers: JSON list of Workspace addresses allowed to click Approve. Same footgun as ReplyCc. Start with one address (the operator) for cutover step 3.
_ChatSpace: spaces/XXXX from the Google Chat space URL. Blank = no cards, no callback function, no URL — the not-live default.
_ChatAudience: The Chat app's GCP project NUMBER (not id). Blank makes the callback reject everything — fail closed.
_ReplyTo: Set to paystatus@circledelivers.com when enabling chat approval, so plain replies return to the group whoever's name the reply carried.
_Timezone: Correctness input, not a logging detail — the gate's tense check judges dates against it. Use the zone name; TZ=EST pins UTC-5 all year and is wrong every summer.
_ScheduleEnabled: Deploy disabled. Invoke manually once, diff against the workstation log, then flip to true and redeploy (cutover step 2).
_AgentEscalationRetryLimit: The same budget for the one escalation reason raised AFTER the agent loop — 'agent produced no draft'. Separate and tighter than EscalationRetryLimit because a pre-model escalation repeats for one id-filter call while this one repeats the whole loop. Listed explicitly even though it matches the template default: the deployed value of a cost knob should be readable here, not inferred from the template.
_EscalationRetryLimit: How many times an ESCALATED message may be re-processed before later runs skip it. An escalation leaves the thread with no draft and no reply, so Gmail's thread-skip never fires on it and the intake window keeps it fetchable for ~96 runs at a 30-minute cadence — and it is not the free outcome it once was, since the LLM id filter runs ahead of every escalation check and 'agent produced no draft' is raised only after the whole agent loop. Above GateBlockRetryLimit on purpose: a transient Transport Pro or CargoTel failure escalates for a reason that fixes itself, and a spent budget does not come back when the cause is fixed. Watch EscalationRetriesExhausted after an outage.
_DailyInputTokenAlarm: Input tokens (cache reads included) in a rolling day above which the LlmSpend alarm fires. A runaway detector, not a budget — the shape it catches is one stuck thread re-billing the agent loop every run. Tighten it once a week of llm_usage log lines says what normal is.
